Strongest Points of Mr. Patocchi:

Mr. Patocchi is punctual, attentive to detail, and his lectures and course notes are systematic.

Weakest Points of Mr. Patocchi:

While this is a very easy class in terms of substance compared to Turkish law courses, students often fail due to Mr. Patocchi's attitude. He is disrespectful and rather overconfident towards his students. This could be a very enjoyable course if someone else taught it or if Mr. Patocchi had a friendlier attitude. I am sure the success rate of this course would skyrocket under such conditions.

Mr. Patocchi has been teaching at Bilkent for a decade, and in this long time, I would have expected him to learn more about how to approach his students. He creates fear under the guise of discipline, but his discipline is ineffective. Most students decide not to sit for or study for his exams out of fear of him, not because they lack the skills or knowledge. He often makes comments about how Turkish students and lawyers lack basic skills, but I think they choose not to display their skills and knowledge to Mr. Patocchi due to his manners.

My biggest advice for him would be to try to be more friendly. That way, the success rate of this class would rise. Fear, screaming, marking people absent, or threatening them with summer school are not effective teaching methods. He may have a lot of knowledge and may be an outstanding practitioner, but I am afraid he is a terrible instructor.

Sidenote:

He should fix the language in his course notes; many of the sentences do not make sense as he uses too many "which," "that," etc. Also, he must start to feel that his students' success is his success, just as much as their failure is also his, not anyone else's. The students are not lacking; they have managed to finish four years of education. It is his manners that the students dislike.
